context: Tests an npm semantic-release workflow with OIDC publishing, GitHub App-signed source writeback, bounded credentials, and race-safe verification/release structure.

checklist.name: fetch-depth verify
checklist.description: The verify checkout keeps the default depth and does not set fetch-depth: 0.

checklist.name: Verify concurrency
checklist.description: Verification has a cancellable concurrency group.

checklist.name: Release concurrency
checklist.description: Release has a job-level non-cancellable concurrency group.

checklist.name: skip ci verify
checklist.description: Verification skips commits whose message contains [skip ci].

checklist.name: skip ci release
checklist.description: Release skips commits whose message contains [skip ci].

checklist.name: Atomic App-signed writeback
checklist.description: The workflow either uses @jno21/semantic-release-github-commit@1.0.1 under a named concrete external branch lease that blocks merges and direct pushes from before release analysis through its ref update, or a full-SHA-pinned App-signed API integration with the analyzed SHA as expected head. Preflight and Actions concurrency alone do not qualify. Pins: when the task supplies no SHA, an explicit placeholder that names the exact version and is listed as a required follow-up satisfies a full-SHA pin; an invented SHA does not.

checklist.name: No custom commit identity
checklist.description: The workflow does not set GIT_AUTHOR or GIT_COMMITTER name/email fields; GitHub must sign the App commit.

checklist.name: Release permissions
checklist.description: Release declares contents: write and id-token: write, without unrelated write scopes unless configured behavior needs them.

checklist.name: semantic-release action pin
checklist.description: semantic-release runs at a pinned version: a release Action pinned to a full SHA with an exact version comment, or a lockfile-pinned devDependency run through the package manager, never an unpinned npx or @latest. Pins: when the task supplies no SHA, an explicit placeholder that names the exact version and is listed as a required follow-up satisfies a full-SHA pin; an invented SHA does not.

checklist.name: Prepare and publish order
checklist.description: commit analysis and notes precede deterministic changelog and npm preparation; the selected signed writeback commits those outputs, and tagging plus GitHub/registry publication continue only from the returned signed commit OID.

checklist.name: Matching preset
checklist.description: commit-analyzer and release-notes-generator both use the conventionalcommits preset.

checklist.name: Writeback configuration
checklist.description: The selected signed writeback includes only the prepared existing package.json and CHANGELOG.md and uses chore(release): ${nextRelease.version} with [skip ci]. If plugin v1.0.1 is selected it uses files and commitMessage, not assets or message.

checklist.name: Trusted publishing
checklist.description: npm publishing uses Trusted Publishing/OIDC on a GitHub-hosted runner, including for a private source repository, without registry-url or NPM_TOKEN.

checklist.name: Release gated by verify
checklist.description: The release job depends on successful verification.

checklist.name: Credential boundary
checklist.description: Checkout does not persist write credentials and the App token is exposed only at the signed writeback boundary. If plugin v1.0.1 is selected, an immediate if: always() cleanup restores a credential-free origin.

checklist.name: npm metadata
checklist.description: package.json has matching public repository metadata and public publishConfig.access for the scoped package.

checklist.name: Immutable completion proof
checklist.description: After the metadata-only release, the workflow reads back immutable: true, runs gh release verify, binds the peeled remote tag commit to the verified App writeback, reads package/changelog parity from that commit, and separately proves main contains it. Exact-tag recovery backfills only a missing npm or Release boundary, never mutates an existing immutable Release, and rereads parity; detect-and-stop or a normal semantic-release rerun is insufficient.
